summary: Server crashes when critical arrow with very high damage value hits an entity
description: The bug When an arrow with a very high damage value (or a really high speed) deals critical damage and hits an entity, the server can crash. [^(20w17a) crash-2020-04-28_22.27.03-server.txt] Description: Ticking entity java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: bound must be positive at java.util.Random.nextInt(Random.java:388) at bdb.a(SourceFile:351) at bdn.a(SourceFile:118) at bdb.h(SourceFile:227) at bdd.h(SourceFile:103) at yr.a(SourceFile:584) at yr$$Lambda$3446/120053388.accept(Unknown Source) at boq.a(SourceFile:577) at yr.a(SourceFile:399) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.b(SourceFile:827) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:766) at enn.a(SourceFile:89) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.run(SourceFile:625) at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745) Reproduction steps - Switch to Survival mode - /execute at @s anchored eyes run summon arrow ~ ~3 ~ {damage:1e100d,crit:1b} The game crashes once the arrow hits you Code analysis 20w17a, Mojang names The fix for MC-87655 made sure, that the damage value used for damage calculation is always = 0. However, if the result of damage speed becomes Integer.MAX_VALUE the result overflows and becomes negative (see MC-181312). If the arrow is dealing critical damage (crit:1b), this negative value is passed to java.util.Random.nextInt(int), the exception seen in the crash report is thrown. If only MC-181312 was fixed, the calculated damage would overflow after adding the critical damage bonus, which might currently not cause any crashes, but could in the future. Therefore, it would make sense to clamp the damage to a maximum (e.g. of Integer.MAX_VALUE / 2, or even smaller) since higher damage will likely never occur in vanilla gameplay anyway and would likely kill any entity instantaneously.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft and create a new world with default settings.  
2. Ensure the game mode is Survival.  
3. Open the chat window.  
4. Run the command ``/execute at @s anchored eyes run summon arrow ~ ~3 ~ {damage:1e100d,crit:1b}``.  
5. Wait approximately 2 seconds for the summoned arrow to fall and hit you.  
6. Observe that the server crashes with an IllegalArgumentException.
Observed Behavior: When a player summons an arrow with an astronomically large damage value (for example using the command /execute at @s anchored eyes run summon arrow ~ ~3 ~ {damage:1e100d,crit:1b}) and the arrow is critical, the server crashes as soon as the projectile contacts an entity; the crash is triggered by a java.lang.IllegalArgumentException stating that the bound must be positive, which originates from a call to java.util.Random.nextInt after the damage calculation overflows into a negative integer. The overflow occurs because the damage speed computation can reach Integer.MAX_VALUE and, when the critical damage bonus is added, the result wraps to a negative number; this negative value is then supplied to the random number generator used for knock‑back and other effects, causing the exception. The stack trace shows the error propagating through bdb.a, bdn.a, bdb.h, bdd.h, yr.a and ultimately the server tick loop, resulting in the server process terminating. Consequently, any attempt to use extremely high‑damage or high‑speed critical arrows in survival mode leads to an immediate server shutdown rather than dealing damage to the target.
Expected Behavior: When a critical arrow with an astronomically high damage value (e.g., damage:1e100d, crit:1b) is summoned and hits an entity, the server should not throw an exception or stop; instead the damage calculation should be clamped to a safe maximum (such as Integer.MAX_VALUE/2) and the arrow should apply that capped damage (or zero if clamped) to the target, after which gameplay continues normally without a crash.
